content.title: About
content.content: Corn chips, flavored are crunchy snack chips made from whole‑grain corn flour and coated with various seasonings (such as cheese, barbecue, sour cream & onion). They have a bold taste, a light salty note and a characteristic crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn chips originated in the United States in the early 20th century as an alternative to potato chips.
Flavoring often relies on natural spices and dry dairy powders.
Corn provides carotenoid antioxidants that give the chips their yellow hue.
In many countries the chips are served with dips like guacamole or salsa.
Baking instead of deep‑frying reduces the fat content of the final product.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn chips contain slowly digestible carbs that provide sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain corn flour adds a modest amount of fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn is a good source of thiamine (B1) and niacin (B3), which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Baking eliminates the formation of trans fatty acids that are common in fried snacks.

items.title: Minimal gluten
items.content: When made with pure corn flour, the chips contain only trace amounts of gluten, making them suitable for people with mild sensitivities.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Flavored chips often contain a significant amount of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even baked chips are energy‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Allergens in seasonings
items.content: Some flavor mixes may include dairy, soy or other common allergens.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature baking can produce acrylamide, a potential toxin.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag, paired with dips (salsa, guacamole, cheese sauce) or used as a crunchy base for salads, tacos and chip‑and‑dip appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life store them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent rancidity.
